Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick responses so far. For the RFP we need two concrete items so our legal and SRE teams can sign off: (1) an exact definition of how Redwood measures monthly availability for hosted inference endpoints (what counts as an outage, which metrics are used, sampling cadence), and (2) the precise workflow for automatic fallbacks and how those interplay with service credit calculations (e.g., if traffic is routed to a lower-capacity region or a quantized model variant).

Can you attach a sample measurement/calculation example (30-day window) and a simple table showing thresholds vs. credit percentages? Also include the types of telemetry you will provide as evidence (raw time-series, synthetic probe logs, request/response traces). We have an excerpt of the RFP attached for context.

We are trying to finalize the SLA section by end of week — appreciate concrete, audit-ready language.

Subject: Re: Availability verification and fallback credit workflow

Danielle —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is our standard (enterprise-ready) response; we can tighten any phrasing to match your legal template. Attaching a short doc with worked examples and a probe config sample.

1) Availability measurement (hosted inference endpoints) — executive summary:
- SLO: Availability is measured as the percentage of successful request attempts accepted by the serving layer over a rolling 30-day window. For hosted API customers we provide a baseline SLO of 99.95% (monthly, rolling).
- What counts as outage: Any request that receives an HTTP 5xx response from the serving runtime, or that times out according to the customer-requested timeout (default 120s), is counted as unavailable. Client-side network failures outside Redwood’s network (e.g., customer LAN outage) are excluded.
- Measurement sources: primary = service telemetry (request/response logs and internal error counters); secondary = synthetic probe coverage (regional probes run every 30s from 12+ vantage points).
- Sampling cadence & aggregation: All requests are recorded. For high-volume customers we provide sampled request logs (1:100 by default) plus aggregated counters at 1-minute resolution. The availability percentage is computed from 1-minute bins over the 30-day window and weighted by request counts.

2) Attribution and multi-region routing:
- Requests are attributed to the customer’s configured endpoint/region. If the customer has cross-region routing enabled, availability is computed per-customer-endpoint using the served-region for each request. We do not double-count: a request served from region B is attributed to region B for that minute.
- Failover behavior: Redwood supports automated region failover and model-variant fallback. If an automated fallback occurs (e.g., primary region degraded and traffic is routed to a secondary region or to a lower-precision model), the request is considered "served" for availability purposes unless it hits an error (5xx) or exceeds the configured timeout. The fallback event itself is recorded in a dedicated event stream and shown in the evidence binder.

3) Service credit calculation (sample table):
- Availability >= 99.95%: No credit
- 99.0% <= Availability < 99.95%: 10% credit of monthly invoice
- 97.0% <= Availability < 99.0%: 25% credit of monthly invoice
- Availability < 97.0%: 50% credit of monthly invoice

Note: For enterprise contracts we can negotiate threshold bands and cap total credit at a mutually agreed maximum; any deviation will be captured in the Master Services Addendum.

4) Evidence and reconciliation process:
- Evidence included for any credit claim: 1) aggregated 1-minute counter export for the impacted 30-day window (CSV), 2) synthetic probe logs (region / probe-id / timestamp / result), 3) request-level error traces (sampled) and the internal incident timeline.
- Reconciliation: Customer raises a credit request with a 60-day discovery window. Redwood will provide the evidence bundle within 7 business days for review. If needed, we will share an anonymized internal incident postmortem (redacted) and enable temporary read-access to a readonly telemetry snapshot for the disputed window.

5) Additional protective clauses:
- Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours notice) and customer misconfiguration are excluded.
- Mitigation: Where an automated fallback preserved correctness but increased latency, we will not issue availability credits for served requests; instead we will classify as a "performance event" and discuss remediation measures and potential one-time concessions in renewal negotiations.

Attachments: redwood-sla-measurement.pdf (worked examples & formulas), probe-config-samples.csv

If this reads OK I can (a) add the exact contract-ready wording for the MSA, and (b) prepare the evidence-binder template we’d provide if a credit is claimed. Karthik / Marissa — flag anything we should tighten before we send this into FinApps legal.

From: Danielle Rivers <procurement@finapps.com>

Subject: Re: Availability verification and fallback credit workflow

Evelyn —

Thanks, this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our SRE team after reviewing the sample:
1) For the attribution model, can you confirm whether the 1-minute bins are computed using UTC boundaries (e.g., 00:00–00:01 UTC) or tenant-local windows? We need deterministic alignment with our own logs.
2) If a fallback to a quantized model variant increases error-rate (incorrect responses), how is that treated? Your note says requests served are "served" for availability — would FinApps still be able to request a credit if the fallback materially degraded accuracy?
3) For the evidence bundle: can you commit to providing the raw CSV export (compressed) plus a signed hash for tamper-evidence? Our auditors require signed artifacts.

We attached an annotated RFP excerpt with preferred contractual language — we are open to minor edits but want the main measurement methodology to remain operationally reproducible.

Thanks,
Danielle

Attachment: finapps-rfp-excerpt-annotated.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FinApps follow-ups on attribution / accuracy / artifacts

Team —

Looping up on FinApps questions (see Danielle's note). Quick proposal so we can reply with a single, contract-ready answer tomorrow morning:
- 1-minute bins: confirm UTC-aligned 1-minute bins (explicitly state format in the MSA exhibit). This is straightforward for our telemetry exports.
- Accuracy/regression during fallback: offer a two-track approach: (A) availability credits are tied strictly to availability (5xx/timeouts). (B) For accuracy regressions caused by an automatic fallback to a lower-precision model, offer a separate remediation: either a one-time invoice credit (negotiated, e.g., up to 15%) or a rollback to previous model variant + priority support. We should allow FinApps to surface a set of golden prompts (up to 200) which we use to validate correctness during the disputed window. That gives the auditors reproducible evidence.
- Signed artifacts: commit to SLS-style signed exports: compressed CSV + SHA256 hash signed by Redwood key (we already do this for some enterprise customers). Add a sentence on retention: raw telemetry snapshot retained for 90 days by default, longer by request.

Marissa / Lauren: can you confirm logistic feasibility on the golden prompts + retention/scan time? If yes, I recommend we OK the above and send a consolidated response. Also propose a small commercial concession for this large deal: reduce the top-tier credit from 50% to 40% in exchange for a 12-month committed usage minimum. We can discuss in the pricing thread.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference
